newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Cosatu plans more strikes on labour bill.
newsitem.headline: S.African Cosatu plans more strikes on labour bill.

text.p: The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) said on Thursday it planned two full-day national strikes plus a programme of regional action in defence of its demands regarding new labour legislation.
"There will be 24-hour strikes on the days that business and labour make their submissions (to parliament on the bill) respectively," Cosatu general secretary Sam Shilowa told a news briefing.
"These actions are intended to send a clear message to business that we are serious about our demands," he said.
Shilowa said there would be separate 24-hour rolling strikes in all regions from August 18 to 21.

Workers in the Eastern Cape would strike on August 18, followed by by those in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga on August 19, the Northern Cape, Free State and Western Cape on August 20, and the Gauteng region around Johannesburg on August 21.
There would be marches and rallies to Business South Africa offices in all regions on the strike days.
Shilowa also announced a nationwide one-hour work stoppage on August 4 between 10.00 a.m. and 11.00 a.m. (0800-0900 GMT).

South African business and labour have clashed on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, with Cosatu -- which has nearly two million members -- calling a one-day national stoppage earlier this month to drive home its claims.
The labour federation is calling for, among other things, a 40-hour working week and six months paid maternity leave.
Shilowa said Cosatu remained available for talks with government on the bill but would not engage with business unless there was a major revision of its position.
The federation would outline its programme of action on Friday at the the National Economic Development and Labour Council negotiating forum, which groups labour, government and business, he added.
